messages:
mia: Heads-up — after upgrading my M1 mac to Sonoma, brew upgraded redwoodctl but I ended up with an x86 binary via Rosetta. When I set REDWOODCTL_LOCALTEST=1 the CLI creates a token then immediately POST -> 401 and loops on refresh.

owen: yikes. Can you paste `file $(which redwoodctl)` and a tiny log?

mia: file output: `redwoodctl: Mach-O 64-bit x86_64`

mia: minimal scrubbed logs:
```
INFO  auth: device flow start
DEBUG token: write /Users/mia/.redwood/tokens/dev.json
INFO  api: POST /token -> 200 access_token issued
INFO  token: saved
INFO  api: POST /token -> 401 invalid_grant
ERROR auth: refresh failed, retrying
```

sam: this matches a previous bug: when the binary runs under Rosetta the process uid/homedir resolution can differ from native arm64 runs, and we end up mixing token stores (host vs brew prefix) or hitting path normalization issues. Also the x86 binary might be reading a different dyld env that affects home lookup.

owen: workaround: `arch -arm64 brew reinstall redwoodctl` or explicitly run the arm64 binary path `/opt/homebrew/bin/redwoodctl` (not the Rosetta symlink). That fixed it for me a few weeks ago.

mia: reinstall with `brew reinstall --build-bottle --force-bottle` did the trick — arm64 binary now and login works.

sam: we should add a CLI-level check: warn if binary arch != system arch and suggest `arch -arm64` on M1/M2. Also add docs to the quickstart and detect mixed-token-store cases and log where tokens are being read/written.

devex-bot: created issue #2520: "redwoodctl: detect Rosetta/x86 installs on Apple Silicon and warn about token path mismatches" (assigned devex).

mia: will add a short note to the mac quickstart and share a tiny gist for the `arch -arm64` workaround. thanks :thumbsup:
